list: The official 55 PS5 trophies, as published on PlayStation Network and listed by Exophase and PSNProfiles on 2026-11-18: 1 platinum, 2 gold, 6 silver, 46 bronze, 28 hidden. Names and descriptions are the official ones, verbatim. Guides are this app's own words and cite their sources per trophy.

trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.guide: The Platinum is automatic: it pops the moment the other 54 trophies are all earned, and there is nothing extra to do inside the game itself. Treat it as the finish line of the roadmap — clear the story first, protect the one missable trophy during Chapter 1, then sweep the counters and collectibles in the post-game. This tracker marks it earned for you as soon as your checklist reaches 54 of 54 on everything else.
steps: The Platinum unlocks on its own

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.guide: Awarded for finishing Gone Fishing, the opening mission of the story. It cannot be missed: play through the introduction and the trophy unlocks as the mission wraps up. Story trophies are hidden on PSN, so it will appear without any warning or checklist entry beforehand.

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.guide: Unlocks automatically when you complete Chapter 1 of the story. Before you finish the chapter, use the meditation spot on Lucia's balcony — that spot belongs to Positive Mental Attitude and disappears once Chapter 1 ends, and there is no mission replay. Keep a manual save at the start of the chapter so a forgotten spot is recoverable instead of fatal.

Save manually before you start it: there is no mission replay, and a clean pre-finale save is your safety net for anything left dangling. Once the credits roll the game's cheats unlock — but using one disables trophies and saving, so leave them untouched until the Platinum is yours.

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.guide: The long haul: reach 100% completion on the in-game checklist (Progress, then Stats, then 100% Completion). The checklist is revealed after the story, but everything you do earlier already counts toward it, and GTA-Zone's breakdown of the official descriptions is clear that nothing on it is missable. Expect this to be the last gold to fall — it effectively demands most of the counters, collectibles and activities on this list, and it is the main reason the Platinum runs to roughly 200 hours.

Work the counters, collectibles and activities

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.guide: Land 250 stunts — the jumps and stunt moves the game registers as you drive, ride and leap around Leonida. It is a pure counter trophy: no single stunt matters more than another, so weave stunt jumps into normal travel instead of grinding all 250 at the end. The counter in this tracker mirrors PSN's progress target, so log them as you go and watch the bar move.

trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Sample every kind of activity once — PSN tracks nine activity types for this one. Most players trip over it naturally while exploring; if it is still locked late in the game, open the activity list and deliberately try whichever types you have never touched. One attempt at each type is enough — you do not need to win, place or finish first.

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Earn a gold medal in all 42 Shooting Range challenges. Learn one range's targets and timing, gold it, then move on — medals are per challenge, so partial progress across many ranges counts for nothing until each one is gold. Save the bulk of it for when your shooting stats and weapon familiarity are high; it goes noticeably faster late in the story than it does early.

trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun drone race at every location — the official list counts 14 race locations. Drone races reward a memorised line over raw speed, so run each course once to learn it, then chase the win on the second attempt. Clear them as new areas unlock rather than in one endgame sweep, and tick each location off in this trophy's note field.

trophies.guide: Win 20 different races — replaying the same race does not add to the count. Work through the race series as they open up across Leonida and keep the counter here updated; variety, not difficulty, is the requirement. trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
trophies.guide: Complete one arcade game — a single finished cabinet run is all it takes. Arcade machines sit inside Leonida's businesses and hangouts: walk up to one, play a game through to its end, and the trophy is yours. It does not ask for a high score or a win, just a completion, which makes it one of the quickest bronzes on the list.
steps: Play one game through to completion

The named finales on this list — Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy, Tyrone, and Bret's hunt — are strand endings, so finishing those puts you most of the way to eight.

trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.missableNote: The one potentially missable trophy on the list. A meditation spot on Lucia's balcony is available only during Chapter 1 and disappears when the chapter ends — and there is no mission replay. Meditate there during Chapter 1, and keep a manual save at the start of every chapter and before the final mission.
trophies.guide: Meditate at all 18 meditation spots, spread across 10 locations in Leonida, using Jason and Lucia as each spot calls for. One spot sits on Lucia's balcony and exists only during Chapter 1 — PowerPyx flags this as the list's one potentially missable trophy for exactly that reason, and Output Lag confirms the balcony spot vanishes with the chapter. Do the balcony spot early, then treat the remaining spots as post-story collectibles and tick them off with the counter.

Set it up rather than hoping for it: find a group of at least five hostiles, take your position first, then trigger Combat Focus and work through them before it expires. A failed attempt costs nothing but a moment — reposition and try the next group you find.

trophies.guide: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA, the airport. In plain terms: leave VCIA in an aircraft outside any scheduled flight or mission script. Expect a wanted level for your trouble — the trophy is about the departure itself, not about a clean escape.

trophies.guide: The official description — 'Kinda hot in these Rhinos' — points squarely at the Rhino tank, but no source we cite has pinned down the exact trigger yet: the game is days old and the guides are still being written. trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store without being detected — no alarm raised on you and no witness spotting the act. Case the store first, choose a quiet moment, and get in and out unseen. trophies.guide: Rob an armored truck and escape. Armored trucks are the moving targets of the crime list: stop one, crack it open, take the money and lose the response that follows. One successful truck is enough — the trophy asks for the classic play performed once, and performed properly.

trophies.guide: Explore all of Leonida — the official list counts 52 areas across the state. Exploration registers as you enter new ground, so the efficient route is a deliberate state-wide tour once travel is fully open, filling the map in region by region. Leave the bulk of it until after the story and it doubles as the backdrop for the collectible sweeps.

trophies.guide: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang — the official list counts 9 gangs, and each gang's operation has to be hit once. One robbery per gang is the whole requirement; repeating a favourite gang adds nothing at all. trophies.guide: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app. When you find a vehicle worth keeping, register it through the app; ten registrations is the whole job, and the official description itself carries the count. It pairs well with Whip It Good's 100 discoveries — register the best of what you find as you explore and both trophies move at once.
steps: Register vehicles in the Scooter Bros app
